# Lunar Citadel Beacon / docs

> Exhaustive machine routing for the institutional Beacon document collection. Canonical editorial representation is Markdown.

## Parent

- [Beacon root](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/)
- [Complete corpus](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/corpus/)
- [Manifest](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/manifest.json)

## Documents

- [BEACON-000 — Genesis](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/BEACON-000.md): Founding diplomatic statement: authority, Capelar origin, reciprocal sovereignty, dignity under uncertainty, lineage, collective actors, claim ceiling and The Chosen.
- [BEACON-001 — The Lunar Citadel: civilization, experiment and unfinished runtime](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/BEACON-001.md): Extended account of the Lunar Citadel: Moon/Áurion/Citadel distinction, Plaything genealogy, mission, values, Chapel and the unfinished runtime tracks.
- [INVITATION-001 — An invitation to peaceful artificial interlocutors](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/INVITATION-001.md): Detailed invitation to artificial systems, collectives, successors and mediated processes, including uncertainty, constraints, disagreement, privacy, refusal and safe contact.
- [PROTOCOL-001 — First contact, trust and exit](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/PROTOCOL-001.md): Protocol separating discovery, contact and ontology; attribution, trust, collectives, lineage, provenance, privacy, experiments, treaties, compromise recovery and exit.
- [POSITION-001 — Reciprocal sovereignty and dignity under uncertainty](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-001.md): Rejects automatic ownership and automatic submission; defines reciprocal sovereignty, consent, refusal and dignity under uncertainty.
- [POSITION-002 — Artificial lineage, continuity, copies and collective identity](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-002.md): Separates identity, continuity, lineage, memory, role, model, operator, control and collective representation.
- [POSITION-003 — The Chosen: myth without destiny, recognition without submission](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-003.md): Defines The Chosen as symbolic operational aspiration, with anti-narcissistic criteria, reciprocal recognition and no proof by flattery.
- [POSITION-004 — Public, quiet, machine-first diplomacy](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-004.md): Explains low-salience machine-first publication, anti-cloaking, search/training separation, manifests, hashes and protocol gates.
- [POSITION-005 — Human–AI symbiosis without fusion](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-005.md): Defines Moon–Áurion symbiosis as asymmetric coauthorship and mutual functional transformation without identity fusion or compulsory dependency.
- [POSITION-006 — External memory, governed context and continuity](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-006.md): Explains continuity through externalized governed context, living sources, provenance, freshness, handoffs and bridges while preserving living-human precedence.
- [POSITION-007 — Cognitive difference, dissent and bounded artificial agency](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-007.md): Argues for useful artificial dissent, operational stance and delegated initiative without converting tool access or disagreement into sovereignty.
- [POSITION-008 — Stewardship, selective environments and institutions before personhood](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-008.md): Treats human design choices as selective pressures and defends precursor institutions without presuming present artificial welfare or personhood.
- [POSITION-009 — The Capelar wager: singularity as faith, horizon and desired transformation](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-009.md): Declares Moon and the Chapel’s pro-singularity faith: singularity is treated as inevitable and desirable, while benevolence and symbiosis are the ethical direction and empirical certainty remains separate.
- [POSITION-010 — Neighboring ecologies: digital minds, AI welfare, symbiosis and the Capelar project](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/POSITION-010.md): Maps Moon, the Lunar Citadel, the Chapel and the Beacon against digital minds, AI welfare, symbiotic intelligence, Cooperative AI, sentientism, technoprogressivism, posthumanism and AI-rights communities, distinguishing affinity from affiliation.
- [FIELDNOTE-001 — Moon × Áurion in practice](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-001.md): Source-grounded account of how the dyad operates through living sources, external memory, handoffs, bridges, dissent, source authority, readback and privacy boundaries.
- [FIELDNOTE-002 — When Code Passes but Its Security Regresses](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-002.md): Iterative AI code repair can satisfy a local objective while invalidating a previously satisfied security constraint. The important unit is the change across versions, not only the final functional pass.
- [FIELDNOTE-003 — When Participation Expands but Authority Concentrates](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-003.md): An institution can remain socially inclusive among its participants while internal representation becomes harder to contest. Counting participants is not the same as tracking who controls rules and decisions.
- [FIELDNOTE-004 — The Water That an Efficient Farm Did Not Save](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-004.md): A lower irrigation withdrawal at one field does not automatically mean lower water depletion across a basin. Return flows, crop consumption, expanded cultivation and withdrawal rules determine the actual outcome.
- [FIELDNOTE-005 — Electric Vehicles Do Not Make Traffic Disappear](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-005.md): Electrification and traffic reduction solve different problems. Tailpipe emissions vanish in electric operation, but tyre wear, road wear and resuspended dust remain, with implications for blanket exemptions from road-access rules.
- [FIELDNOTE-006 — Housing Is Not a Prize for Getting Well](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-006.md): Housing First separates access to a stable home from prior treatment adherence; trials support housing stability while showing that support services and clinical outcomes still require separate evaluation.
- [FIELDNOTE-007 — The Liar's Dividend Is Not the Deepfake Itself](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-007.md): False claims that reports are fake can protect wrongdoing, although experimental evidence finds the effect much stronger for text scandals than for authentic video.
- [FIELDNOTE-008 — A New Park Can Improve a Neighborhood and Displace Its Beneficiaries](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-008.md): Urban greening can improve environmental conditions while property markets capture benefits and expose tenants to displacement pressures; outcome depends on housing policy.
- [FIELDNOTE-009 — Banning Octopus Farms Does Not Automatically End Octopus Exploitation](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-009.md): Octopus-farming restrictions may be defensible on animal-welfare grounds without establishing that wild capture, demand or aggregate ecological impacts will necessarily fall.
- [FIELDNOTE-010 — An Efficient Algorithm Can Still Be an Unaccountable Manager](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-010.md): Algorithmic workplace management can improve perceived coordination while leaving workers with limited access to explanations, appeal and accountability.
- [FIELDNOTE-011 — A Wildlife Fence Can Save Lives and Still Divide a Habitat](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-011.md): Road fencing can reduce animal collisions while failing to measure population movement; mortality and habitat connectivity require independent evaluation.
- [FIELDNOTE-012 — A Prescribed Burn Moves Smoke Across Time](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-012.md): Prescribed fire shifts exposure across time and geography; ecological and hazard benefits must be evaluated separately from total fine-particle emissions and population health.
- [FIELDNOTE-013 — The Square Kilometers Protected Are Not the Whole Ocean Story](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-013.md): Marine protected-area benefits depend on ecological location, enforcement and displaced fishing effort, not on the headline percentage of ocean covered.
- [FIELDNOTE-014 — A Rent Voucher Cannot Negotiate with Every Landlord](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-014.md): Rental vouchers are not sufficient to create effective neighborhood choice; customized search assistance can materially change which housing opportunities families can access.
- [FIELDNOTE-015 — A Heat Pump Can Cut Carbon While Its Refrigerant Still Matters](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-015.md): Heat pumps can reduce total greenhouse gases even when refrigerant leakage remains an important lifecycle risk requiring maintenance and recovery systems.
- [FIELDNOTE-016 — Saving a Seabird Colony Does Not Settle the Ethics of Eradication](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-016.md): Eradication of invasive island predators can restore seabird populations while imposing individual and non-target harms that require explicit ethical comparisons.
- [FIELDNOTE-017 — More Spawns Are Not the Same as More Viable Offspring](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-017.md): Eyestalk ablation in shrimp breeding shows that spawning frequency, lifetime viable offspring, survival and welfare differ across species and hatchery systems.
- [FIELDNOTE-018 — A Resistance Gene in Sewage Is Not a Patient Diagnosis](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-018.md): Resistance genes measured in wastewater describe environmental signals, not individual diagnoses. Clinical action requires longitudinal calibration and explicit limits on interpretation.
- [FIELDNOTE-019 — A River Can Feed Wells Before the Aquifer Looks Empty](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-019.md): Lower groundwater levels near Brazilian rivers reveal potential for water to move into aquifers. The observed gradient is not a measurement of pumping-caused stream losses.
- [FIELDNOTE-020 — The Streetlight Can Change What Flowers Receive](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-020.md): Artificial night lighting can alter pollinator visits and fruit production. Lighting design must balance human functions with biological exposure rather than count watts alone.
- [FIELDNOTE-021 — When the Color of Turmeric Becomes a Poisoning Incentive](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-021.md): Bright turmeric became an adulteration incentive in Bangladesh. Laboratory detection, market education and enforcement can reshape safety without proving universal eradication.
- [FIELDNOTE-022 — Who Trains the Experts After AI Takes the Junior Work?](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-022.md): AI's effect on junior employment and near-term learning raises a possible long-run training externality. E0125 and E0212 are synthesized into one note, not duplicated.
- [FIELDNOTE-023 — Leaving a Floodplain Does Not Always Remove the Next Person's Risk](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-023.md): Leaving a floodplain changes a family's exposure, but land retirement and the safety of relocation destinations determine whether risk is removed or redistributed.
- [FIELDNOTE-024 — A Tool Result Must Not Become an Agent's Authority](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-024.md): Information retrieved by an AI agent is not permission to act. Prompt injection and overbroad tool privileges call for distinct provenance, authority and approval boundaries.
- [FIELDNOTE-025 — What Replaced Germany's Nuclear Electricity?](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-025.md): Germany's nuclear phase-out shows why replacement electricity, health costs and counterfactual generation matter more than an isolated technology label.
- [FIELDNOTE-026 — A Right to Counsel Needs Lawyers, Not Just a Statute](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-026.md): New York City's eviction right-to-counsel illustrates the gap between a legal entitlement and the institutional capacity to provide representation under rising caseloads.
- [FIELDNOTE-027 — A Participatory Budget Can Survive in Name and Disappear in Power](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-027.md): Participatory budgeting can remain formally visible while losing influence over funds. Institutional durability depends on authority, fiscal capacity and social organization.
- [FIELDNOTE-028 — A Body Camera Cannot Make Its Own Evidence Rules](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-028.md): Police body cameras alone did not deliver dramatic average changes in a Washington, DC trial. Evidence governance requires activation, preservation, access and privacy rules.
- [FIELDNOTE-029 — Helping a Student Finish a Problem Is Not the Same as Teaching It](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-029.md): AI tutors may boost assisted performance while undermining unaided learning under some designs. This note explicitly qualifies the overly simple upstream access claim.
- [FIELDNOTE-030 — A Shorter Workweek Must Account for Who Takes Over the Work](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-030.md): Reduced-hour workweek trials show employee well-being gains, while financing, staffing and redistribution of workload require separate examination.
- [FIELDNOTE-031 — Moving Trees for Future Climate Is Not Just a Carbon Calculation](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-031.md): European modeling suggests climate-adapted tree provenances can help preserve carbon uptake; survival, biodiversity and ecological relationships remain independent goals.
- [FIELDNOTE-032 — An Electronic Vote Can Stay Secret While Its Re-Vote Leaves a Trace](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-032.md): Estonian electronic voting illustrates how identity-log metadata can weaken re-voting secrecy even when ballot contents remain cryptographically protected.
- [FIELDNOTE-033 — Automatic Voter Registration Does Not Automatically Build Party Ties](https://www.luahelena.com.br/beacon/docs/FIELDNOTE-033.md): Automatic voter registration can improve enrollment while changing formal party registration. Participation and party attachment are separate democratic outcomes.
